extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, authors, reviewers, and funders interested in adopting or submitting Registered Reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required features for the Registered Reports publishing format, including Stage 1/Stage 2 manuscript requirements, reviewer assessment criteria, editorial workflow, and funder-journal partnership considerations. Intended to help journals, editors, authors, reviewers and funders implement and evaluate Registered Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review prior to observing outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review occurs prior to observing the outcomes of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an article type to qualify as a Registered Report, the journal policy must ensure that peer review happens before data collection or before outcomes are known. This is the defining feature of the format.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-principle acceptance (IPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts that survive pre-study peer review receive an in-principle acceptance that will not be revoked based on the outcomes, but only on failings of quality assurance, following through on the registered protocol, or unresolvable problems in reporting clarity or style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPA provides a virtual guarantee of publication if the authors conduct the experiment in accordance with their approved protocol. It should not be revoked for null or negative results; revocation is limited to failures of quality checks, protocol non-adherence, or reporting problems. Journals sometimes publish a Withdrawn Registration if authors withdraw after IPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 manuscript required content
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of Registered Reports initially submit a Stage 1 manuscript that includes an Introduction, Methods, and the results of any pilot experiments that motivate the research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 1 should provide sufficient detail (e.g., step-by-step account of procedures and analysis plan) to allow rigorous pre-study peer review and to permit reviewers to assess feasibility, power, and validity of proposed tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 manuscript required content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Following data collection, authors resubmit a Stage 2 manuscript that includes the Introduction and Methods from the original submission plus the Results and Discussion. The Results section includes the outcome of the pre-registered analyses together with any additional unregistered analyses in a separate section titled 'Exploratory Analyses'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage 2 must preserve the originally approved Introduction and Methods; exploratory analyses are allowed but must be clearly separated from pre-registered confirmatory analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear separation of confirmatory vs exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The RR model requires that the Results section distinguishes those analyses that were pre-registered and confirmatory from those that were post hoc and exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No constraint is placed on reporting exploratory analyses, but authors must clearly identify which tests were pre-registered. The recommended format is a separate 'Exploratory Analyses' section for unregistered tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and analysis code sharing encouraged/required
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged or required to share their data on a public and freely accessible archive such as OSF or Figshare and are encouraged to share data analysis scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data archiving increases transparency and enables meta-analysis and detection of data problems. Some journals may mandate data and code availability upon publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specify outcome-neutral checks and quality controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 review should include consideration of sufficient outcome-neutral conditions (e.g., absence of floor or ceiling effects; positive controls; other quality checks) to ensure that the results obtained are able to test the stated hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcome-neutral checks must be pre-specified at Stage 1 and independent of the primary outcome measures. At Stage 2, reviewers assess whether the data pass these approved checks; failure of a crucial quality check could be grounds for rejection at Stage 2. (Quoted example: Royal Society Open Science Stage 1 Criterion 6.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate statistical power reporting or justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 submissions should include a statistical power analysis based on plausible effect sizes, pilot data, or a minimal effect size of theoretical interest to determine a priori power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the likely effect size is unknown, authors can use pilot results, related prior work, minimal meaningful effect sizes, corrected peeking approaches, or Bayesian methods with explicit priors. The RR model disfavors underpowered experiments and encourages combining resources to increase power where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specify decision trees for contingent analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyses depend on the results (i.e., decisions contingent on data), the pre-registration must specify the decision tree (e.g., 'If A is observed then adopt analysis A1; if B is observed then adopt analysis B1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every step must be hardwired; specifying the contingency rules satisfies pre-registration requirements. Exploratory analyses that cannot be specified in advance are allowed but must be labeled as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and commencement guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must certify that all necessary support (e.g., funding, facilities) and approvals (e.g., ethics) are in place and that the researchers could start promptly following in-principle acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guarantee is intended because IPA assumes the study can commence; journals may allow agreed delayed commencement dates. Funders–journal partnerships rely on such assurances to align funding and IPA decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 triage and structured review of fixed criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should triage Stage 1 submissions (often via a dedicated team of associate editors) to ensure submissions meet basic requirements (e.g., adequate power analysis, sufficient detail in proposed analyses) before in-depth review; reviewers are often asked to assess manuscripts against a number of fixed criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structured reviewer assessments help ensure attention to pre-specified criteria (importance, methodological rigor, feasibility, quality checks). Templates of reviewer invitation letters and decision letters are provided as resources to implement structured reviews even if submission systems cannot implement fielded forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specify positive controls and manipulation checks where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and editors can pre-specify positive controls, manipulation checks or other standards for assessing study quality at Stage 1; these tests must be independent of primary outcomes and pre-specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including such checks allows assessment at Stage 2 whether data genuinely test hypotheses (e.g., verify intervention administration or measurement validity). If pre-specified checks fail, this may justify rejection at Stage 2 despite IPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted handling of sequential and multi-experiment plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The RR model welcomes sequential registrations in which authors add experiments at Stage 1 via an iterative mechanism and complete them at Stage 2; authors may also submit Stage 1 manuscripts that include multiple parallel experiments or a sequence of preliminary unregistered experiments followed by preregistered ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each completed cycle (experiment) can be guaranteed publication as accepted; flexibility is allowed for series or iterative designs so long as pre-specification and contingency plans are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable alternative statistical approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: If effect sizes cannot be estimated, authors may adopt NHST approaches with corrected peeking or Bayesian methods that specify a prior distribution of possible effect sizes rather than a single point estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines accept multiple statistically principled approaches for handling uncertainty about effect size, provided the approach and rules (e.g., stopping rules or priors) are pre-specified in Stage 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results Blind Peer Review requirements (allied initiative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Results Blind Peer Review: in the first stage, authors include a full manuscript for the abstract, introduction, and methods without the results and discussion sections; the submitted manuscript must not indicate information about the outcome-relevant results. The methods must contain a complete analysis plan of what is to be included in the full article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission passes initial review, authors then submit a complete manuscript for second stage review to confirm that the final report adequately addresses reviewer concerns. Outcome-irrelevant results may be reported to demonstrate quality checks (e.g., manipulations effective). This is an allied but distinct format from Registered Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triage and editorial discretion on importance and methodological stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals may apply stringent Stage 1 review to restrict provisional acceptance to studies judged to be informative and important; IPA is not an obligation to accept methodologically weak but interesting studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors can pre-select Stage 1 RRs that address the most important questions; offering RRs as an author option (not mandatory) allows editorial discretion by sub-discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome-neutral criteria must be independent of primary outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome-neutral criteria (e.g., absence of floor/ceiling effects, positive controls) must be independent of the primary outcome measures and pre-specified at Stage 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These checks ensure data can legitimately test hypotheses. Their independence preserves protection against outcome-contingent 'quality' definitions that could otherwise reintroduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 acceptable materials registry or preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors or editors can register accepted Stage 1 protocols by selecting 'Registered Report Protocol Preregistration' on the OSF Registry (or appropriate registry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of public registries documents the accepted protocol and supports transparency. The site provides templates and a checklist to help craft effective Stage 1 submissions.
